issues.description: The template Lecture.java declares addGuestStudents with two parameters (int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput), whereas the problem statement (including the UML) and the solution expect a single-parameter method addGuestStudents(int). This mismatch between the template stub and the specified API will confuse students about the required signature and prevents a direct implementation that matches the specification/tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template method signature to match the specification: replace public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput) with public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) { /* TODO */ }. Alternatively, update the problem statement/UML to document the additional boolean parameter if that was intended.

issues.description: The problem statement and solution expect an addGuestStudents(int) method, but the template declares addGuestStudents(int, boolean). The extra boolean parameter in the template method signature creates a mismatch between the required API (addGuestStudents(int)) described in the exercise and the starter code, causing compilation confusion and making it unclear which method students should implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template method signature to match the problem and solution: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) — remove the boolean parameter (or provide an overload delegating to the single-argument method) so the starter code matches the expected API.
